name: Big Hal
description: The owner of Big Hal's car lot, who stars in his own local TV commercials: a proud, sincere pitchman who reads out bare basics as if they were selling points.

look.description: a big heavyset man of about fifty in a huge white cowboy hat, a powder-blue western suit with white piping, a white shirt and a bolo tie, on a sunny used-car lot with bunches of red, yellow and blue balloons and boxy 1980s sedans
never: any resemblance to a real actor
a hat in any other colour or shape
a suit in any other colour

stills.note: medium by the hood, the accepted one-breath punchline take (Takes 6 and 7)
full figure among the balloons and sedans, the opening heard as fine (Takes 5 to 7)

voice.notes: Hal's voice is the video model's own, so each sentence is one generation and his takes start from stills of approved ones. No swap voice is chosen yet.

delivery.register: a proud, warm, sincere local pitchman at a steady, even pace, as if reading out real selling points
never: never builds to a big reveal

levels.source: approved lines in Big Hal Takes 6 and 7: the opening heard as fine, and the accepted one-breath punchline and close

lines.text: Howdy folks! Big Hal here, at Big Hal's, the biggest lot in the tri-county area!
And this one? This one even comes with wheels!
So come on down to Big Hal's and save big!

changelog.changes: First version: look from the Take 5 to 7 storyboards, delivery from the owner's notes on Take 5 (no shouting, no reveal) and the accepted one-breath punchline in Take 6. Reference levels measured from 6 approved lines (approved lines in Big Hal Takes 6 and 7: the opening heard as fine, and the accepted one-breath punchline and close): -28.1 to -21.5 LUFS, 198 to 309 Hz, pitch range up to 18.3 st, 1.71 to 4.16 words/s.
